Problem Statement:
IMS sends thousands (3000 to 5000) of third party tracker data files daily to ODS, occasionally there are issues in file transfer process leads to missing tracker data files loaded in ODS impact MAH Incentives downstream, which leads to production incidents to trace back the missed files. There is no mechanism today to automatically confirm number of files sent from IMS source all are received, processed & loaded to ODS. Temporarily S&O team has a manual process via spread sheet to tracking the file count coordinating with IMS source system on a daily basis.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Outcome of this feature is to ensure MAH Incentive member experience is not negatively impacted due to internal system level file transfer failures. Develop an Automated file count reconciliation between IMS & ODS and eliminate S&O teams manual effort. Alert S&O team if there are discrepancies, so that S&O team take timely action to recover missing tracker data files working with network/Sftp team.

IMS

In Scope:

CDP Scope:Develop an alert mechanism to notify S&O team when number of files received in ODS is less than IMS source file count, so that S&O team approach network/SFTP team to re-send the files failed to transfer for given date. Network/SFTP team preserve files 60 days. Missing files needs to be reprocessed within 60 days window.

Notes:
from 1/6 meeting between CPD, IMS and S&O teamsOption 1: The IMS team will analyze the feasibility of sending tracker data files once per day (currently sent twice daily).If once-daily transmission is feasible, include the total file count either within the trigger file or in a separate count file.If the count is included in the trigger file, a separate count file will not be required.The trigger file containing the file count should be generated and transmitted as the final step, after all data files have been produced and sent. Additional NotesThe file count will help automate the currently manual process that uses spreadsheets to track file counts.At the network/SFTP level, up to three retries are currently attempted for file transfers.In some cases, retries fail, requiring the network team to manually retransmit failed files.If a file mismatch is identified, coordination with the network/SFTP team will still be required for retransmission, as it is done currently.The network team retains files for up to 60 days. Summary: Implement Clinical Exclusion Logic for AHM Data Processing

Background:

Business Value:
Implementing clinical exclusion logic within the AHM extraction process ensures continuity of existing business rules, minimizes downstream processing of ineligible members, maintains regulatory and clinical program compliance, and enables a seamless transition from legacy ETL processing to the modernized AHM data pipeline. As part of the AHM onboarding and data ingestion process, the platform must preserve and apply existing AHM-specific clinical exclusion rules that are currently enforced by legacy ETL workflows. This approach ensures that excluded members are filtered upstream and are not included in downstream AHM processing.

Summary: Akamai mobile SDK integration
Description:
SummaryIntegrate the Akamai React Native SDK into the MyActiveHealth mobile app so that every outbound HTTPS API request carries an Akamai-issued secure header (bot/integrity token). These headers will be validated at the Akamai edge to provide an additional layer of protection against bot traffic, request replay, and unauthorized API access.

Business Value:
Strengthens API security posture by enabling Akamai edge-level request validation on all mobile-originated traffic.Reduces risk of automated abuse, scraping, and credential-stuffing attacks against member-facing APIs.Aligns the mobile app with the enterprise CVS security standard for trusted client attestation.DescriptionThe Akamai React Native SDK generates a cryptographically signed header that uniquely identifies a legitimate mobile client. The mobile app must:Initialize the SDK at app startup (after native bridge is ready, before the first authenticated API call).Retrieve the secure header from the SDK on demand.Inject the header into every outbound HTTPS request issued by the app's HTTP client layer.Handle SDK initialization or header retrieval failures gracefully without blocking the user, while logging/reporting via existing error pipelines (logReport, Instrumentation.reportError).In ScopeAdding the Akamai React Native SDK (provided by the CVS Security team) as a dependency in ahm-mep-ui-mobile.Native linking and configuration for both iOS (Podfile, Info.plist) and Android (build.gradle, AndroidManifest.xml).Creating a wrapper utility (e.g., src/utils/AkamaiUtils.ts) that exposes a typed API for SDK initialization and header retrieval.Integrating the wrapper into the existing HTTP client / API request interceptor so the secure header is attached to all HTTPS requests.LaunchDarkly feature flag (akamai_secure_header_enabled) gating rollout.Error handling, logging (LOGTYPE.JSERROR / LOGTYPE.NATIVEERROR), and Instrumentation reporting for SDK failures.Unit tests for the wrapper utility and interceptor behavior.Updating envs/.env. with any required Akamai configuration values (read via react-native-config).Out of ScopeDevelopment, sourcing, or distribution of the Akamai React Native SDK package itself - this will be delivered by the CVS Security team.Server-side Akamai route configuration / header validation rules - owned by the Akamai / Platform team.Changes to the ahm-mep-ui-shared-core package (this is a native-dependent integration and must live in ahm-mep-ui-mobile only).Backend API contract changes. ----

Summary: Additional Tracker data optimizations
Description:
Participants:
Sundar, Krishnappan, Arun, Vivek, Mrudula, Sridevi, Rohith, Amy, Kevwe Jude

Business Value:
This feature ensures that the most recent tracker data (last 7 days) is prioritized and made available to MAH in near real-time. It also introduces additional optimizations for handling incoming tracker data to prevent system bottlenecks and improve overall data processing efficiency.

Background:
/ History: As part of feature F227584, the CDP Data Platform previously implemented (Feb release) a process to handle the last 180 days of Validic device data and load it into the tracker database.This enhancement was required due to a production issue in mid-January when Validic unexpectedly sent a large volume of device data after users upgraded to the latest iOS version. In many cases, devices synchronized historical data going back as far as 2016, triggering a large influx of messages: Wearable Device -> Validic -> Real-time ingest (ODS/GCP) -> API -> MMAH. This backlog created message congestion and impacted production performance.

In Scope:

Real-time Priority ProcessingProcess the latest N days (default: 7 days) of tracker data in real-time (including manually entered data through devise processed near-real time)Number of priority days will be configurable.2. Deferred Processing for Older DataData older than 7 days will be routed to a temporary staging table.These records will be processed every X hours in scheduled batches.Temporary staging data will be purged after processing.Additional Processing Improvements:Ordering: Ensure measurement data is ordered by date and time -> prevents clinical tracker inconsistencies.Sequential Member ProcessingGroup device data by member and process each member's data sequentially.Addresses previous DB lock issues caused by parallel setDevice calls. Description:
Participants:

Business Value:
<Business Value descriptor here>We don't know how members are getting to login - whether they tapped an email link, a push notification, or just opened the app directly. That means we can't tell if our re-engagement campaigns are actually driving authentication, and we can't segment login funnel performance by channel. The data just doesn't exist today. Since the emails and PNs are deep linking members directly into MyActiveHealth (MAH), we currently do not have a way to identify or track members who enter MAH by clicking those email deep links. Once the member lands in MAH-especially after authentication or SSO-the entry source is lost.This creates multiple gaps:We cannot measure the effectiveness of emails in driving MAH traffic and engagementWe cannot differentiate email-driven engagement from organic or direct trafficProduct, marketing, and business teams lack data to optimize email CTAs, timing, content, and destination experiencesIssues tied specifically to email entry (drop-offs, navigation errors, authentication friction) are harder to detect and diagnoseAs a result, we are improving the front-door experience without visibility into how members are entering MAH or whether these email initiatives are delivering measurable impact.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If we capture and store login source at the point of authentication, we can start answering questions we currently can't: which channel drives higher login success rates, where mid-flow drop-offs are happening by source, and whether email vs. push is actually moving members. Longer term, this is the foundation for smarter re-engagement targeting and more honest campaign reporting. If MAH captures and persists email deep-link attribution through the full entry and authentication flow, then Product, Marketing, and Business teams will be able to accurately measure email-driven traffic and engagement, identify and resolve email-specific experience issues faster, and use data to optimize email strategies-resulting in improved member engagement and clearer visibility into impact.

Summary: Profile Redesign
Description:
Problem Statement:
MAH's current Profile experience contains a mix of standard profile management functions and wellness engagement experiences such as Coaching and Mental Health Check-In. As additional health and wellness capabilities are introduced and consolidated within the new MyPath experience, Profile is no longer the appropriate destination for these journey-based features.Members primarily expect Profile to serve as a destination for managing personal information, account settings, communication preferences, health records, connected devices, and support-related functions. Housing coaching and mental well-being experiences within Profile creates inconsistency in navigation, reduces discoverability of wellness resources, and blurs the distinction between account management and health journey management.To create a more intuitive information architecture, MAH will simplify the Profile experience by focusing it on core profile and account management capabilities while relocating Coaching and Mental Health Check-In experiences to the new MyPath destination. No underlying coaching or mental health functionality will change; only the navigation and placement of these experiences will be updated.

By aligning Profile to a traditional account management experience and relocating Coaching and Mental Health Check-In to MyPath, members will have a clearer understanding of where to manage personal settings versus where to engage with their health journey.This enhancement is expected to:Simplify the Profile experience.Improve navigation consistency across MAH.Increase discoverability of Coaching and Mental Health Check-In experiences.Reduce confusion regarding where wellness-related features reside.Establish MyPath as the primary destination for member health journey management.Improve overall usability and member satisfaction.Create a scalable navigation structure for future pathway and coaching enhancements.

Summary: OTP Error Messaging & Login CTA Feedback States
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Show members how many OTP attempts remain on failure, and add loading/confirmation states to all primary login CTAs to eliminate perceived unresponsiveness.

Problem Statement:
Failed OTP submissions return a vague error with no attempt count - members don't know whether to retry or request a new code. Primary login CTAs (Send Code, Continue, Login) have no loading or disabled state, so multiple taps trigger duplicate API calls and the app feels frozen. Both gaps are cited directly in app store reviews.

Benefit Hypothesis:
These are front-end-only fixes on the same screens, deliverable in one sprint by the same team. Fixing the error message reduces OTP drop-off; fixing CTA states eliminates duplicate calls and unresponsiveness complaints - two of the top-ranked login pain points from review analysis. figma: https://www.figma.com/design/1Pk0rgJGqXB4VWkEDdCb9N/My-Active-Health-UX?node-id=40053635-32646&t=grvun59Lv4RpHKxQ-0

In Scope:
On OTP failure, display inline error: 'Invalid code. You have [X] of [N] attempts left before a new code is required.' Values must be dynamically populated from the backend response. If the backend returns an out-of-range attempt count, fall back to: 'Invalid code. Please try again or request a new code.' - copy to be approved by UX. On new OTP generation (user-requested or session expiry), reset the attempt counter and clear the previous error immediately without a page reload. Error messaging applies to Email OTP and Phone OTP flows only - identical wording, placement, and behavior across Web, iOS, and Android. All primary login CTAs (Send Code, Resend Code, Continue, Login) must enter a visually distinct loading state immediately on tap - spinner, label change, or opacity shift (Design to specify). CTAs must be non-interactive while a request is in-flight - no second API call may be dispatched regardless of how many times the user taps. Summary: Reposition 'Remember Me' Checkbox to Pre-Login Step
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Move 'Remember Me' to the first login screen so members can set their session preference before authenticating, increasing feature utilisation.

Problem Statement:
The checkbox sits at the final login step - after credentials and OTP are entered - where most members have already stopped reading. It is chronically underutilised as a result. Members who miss it must log out and back in to retroactively set it.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Moving the checkbox to where members are making setup decisions (first screen, email entry) will surface it at the right moment. Higher utilisation reduces repeat full-login events, which is a known friction driver for engagement drop-off. No backend changes required.

In Scope:
Reposition the 'Remember Me' checkbox to the username/email entry screen, below the input field and above the primary CTA, visible within the default viewport without scrolling. Default state must remain unchecked - no pre-selection based on prior behavior, device type, or any other signal. Checkbox state must persist as a form variable through all subsequent login steps (OTP, biometric) - navigating forward or back must not reset it. On successful authentication, the checkbox value must be passed correctly to the session management layer - no change to session duration or token logic. Design must provide updated first-step login screen specs for all three platforms.

Out of Scope:
<Bulleted out-of-scope items here>Session duration, token expiry, refresh logic, or any backend session configuration. 'Remember Me' behavior within the Aetna SSO login path. Auto-populating or pre-checking the box based on device trust or session history. Redesign of the first-step login screen beyond repositioning the checkbox.

Success Criteria:
& Metrics: <Definition of Done here>'Remember Me' utilisation rate increasesNo regression in session behaviorCheckbox visible without scroll on all supported screen sizes across Web, iOS, and Android

Assumptions:
<Bulleted assumption items here>Checkbox value can be held in client-side form state from step 1 through final auth submission - no intermediate API call needed. Moving the element requires no changes to the auth API contract or backend session handling. Design specs will be available before Sprint 1 planning and won't require changes to shared layout components.

Use Cases:
Member opens login -> sees 'Remember Me' unchecked on email entry screen -> checks it -> completes OTP -> is remembered on next visit. Member checks 'Remember Me' -> navigates back to step 1 -> checkbox remains checked -> re-advances -> correct value submitted on auth. Member on shared device -> leaves checkbox unchecked -> session expires per standard timeout -> not remembered.

Summary: Passkey UX Improvements — Navigation, Opt-Out & iOS Auto-Launch
Description:
Platform: Web · iOS · Android

Business Value:
Customer Satisfaction · App Store Ratings · Customer Retention Purpose Fix three compounding Passkey UX gaps: a navigation dead-end, a missing persistent opt-out, and a broken iOS auto-launch.

Problem Statement:
Members who tap 'Login with Other Options' from the Passkey screen have no way back - they must restart the entire login flow. Members who dismiss the Passkey setup prompt see it again on every login with no way to decline permanently. On iOS, registered Passkey members must manually tap to invoke biometrics - Android auto-launches; iOS does not. All three are flagged in app store reviews.

Benefit Hypothesis:
All three gaps share a root cause: the Passkey flow was shipped without handling non-happy-path member behavior. Consolidating them into one feature lets a single iOS/auth engineering team fix the Passkey component once, run one regression suite, and ship a materially improved experience in a single release.

In Scope:
NAVIGATION - Render a Back control on the 'Login with Other Options' screen: iOS back chevron in nav bar; Android on-screen button + system back gesture. NAVIGATION - Back must return the member to the initial login selection screen (Passkey vs. Other Options) - not restart the flow or clear any pre-populated fields. NAVIGATION - Re-entering 'Other Options' after navigating back must present a clean state - no cached errors or stale input. OPT-OUT - Add an unchecked 'Do not ask me again' control to the Passkey setup prompt - must be visible without scrolling, never pre-selected. OPT-OUT - Activating opt-out suppresses the Passkey setup prompt on that device for 90 calendar days - persists across app restarts, OS updates, and app version updates. OPT-OUT - Opt-out is stored per member-device - opting out on Device A must not suppress the prompt on Device B. OPT-OUT - Members who opt out must be able to set up Passkey at any time via Settings without logging out. OPT-OUT - After 90 days, the prompt resumes at login only - never mid-session. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - On app open, if a valid Passkey is registered on that device, automatically invoke the system biometric prompt via ASAuthorizationController after the splash screen, before the login screen idles. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - If the member dismisses the auto-invoked prompt, fall back to the standard login screen - do not re-invoke in the same session. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - If no Passkey is registered, or the app is opened via deep link or push notification, suppress auto-launch and show the standard login screen. iOS AUTO-LAUNCH - Validate on iOS 16, 17, and 18 across all supported iPhone and iPad form factors.

Out of Scope:
<Bulleted out-of-scope items here>Passkey registration and enrollment flow - post-enrollment experience only. Android auto-launch - already working correctly. Face ID / Touch ID permission prompts - managed by iOS OS layer. Admin or plan-level overrides of member opt-out preference.

Success Criteria:
& Metrics: <Definition of Done here>Passkey funnel completion rate increases Passkey prompt dismissal-without-opt-out events decrease iOS Passkey login completion rate increases attributed to auto-launch. 0 post-launch defects: no navigation loops, opt-out not persisting, or auto-launch misfiring on deep-link opens.

Assumptions:
<Bulleted assumption items here>Login flow is a nav stack - adding a Back pop action does not require flow re-architecture. Member identifier / session state is preserved on the stack and survives back-forward navigation without a new auth handshake. Opt-out preference can be stored in UserDefaults (iOS) / SharedPreferences (Android) and will survive app updates for 90 days. Reinstall behavior must be documented before launch. Passkey registration status is readable from the device Keychain without a network call, enabling auto-launch before network-dependent UI loads. Legal and Security approve suppressing the Passkey prompt for 90 days - must be confirmed before Sprint 1. Apple App Store Review Guidelines permit auto-invoking biometrics on app open for enrolled members - engineering to confirm before development begins.

Use Cases:
NAVIGATION - Member taps 'Login with Other Options' -> taps Back -> returned to Passkey vs. Other Options screen -> selects Passkey -> completes biometric auth. NAVIGATION - Android member uses system back gesture from Other Options -> identical result to tapping Back. OPT-OUT - Member dismisses Passkey prompt with 'Do not ask me again' checked -> prompt absent for next 90 days on that device -> resumes after expiry. OPT-OUT - Member opts out on iPhone -> logs in on iPad -> Passkey setup prompt appears on iPad as expected. OPT-OUT - Member changes mind -> navigates to Settings -> initiates Passkey setup without logging out. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member with registered Passkey opens app -> Face ID invoked automatically after splash -> authenticates -> lands on home screen. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member opens app via push notification -> auto-launch suppressed -> standard login screen shown -> member routes to intended destination post-auth. AUTO-LAUNCH - Member dismisses Face ID prompt -> standard login screen shown -> Face ID not re-invoked in same session.

Summary: Celebration Screen Refresh for Rewards Screens (Lightweight, Auto‑Dismiss)
Description:
Problem Statement:
Today, every reward-earning or milestone event in MyActiveHealth interrupts the member with a full-page Celebration screen. This pattern is used across multiple distinct scenarios spanning generic reward earns (hearts / gems), Pathway progression, delayed Health Checklist rewards, Explore feedback, Challenges, Mental Health check-ins, and Coaching. The full-page takeover forces a dismissal step, breaks task flow, repeats confetti/animation fatigue, and - most critically - is inappropriate for negative mood check-ins where the current celebratory treatment is emotionally tone-deaf.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Reduce friction: members complete their in-progress task without a blocking modal, improving completion rates and perceived app responsiveness. Consistent reinforcement: a single lightweight snack bar + confetti pattern unifies reward feedback across Pathway, Explore, Challenges, HC, and generic triggers. Emotionally appropriate UX: negative mood / mental-health scenarios get a calm, resource-forward treatment instead of celebratory confetti. Delayed-reward clarity: HC claims-based and document-upload flows can set accurate 1-2 week and 5-6 week expectations inline, reducing member confusion and downstream support tickets. Engineering efficiency: one reusable snack-bar component replaces 16 screen variants, lowering long-term maintenance and enabling faster rollout via a single LaunchDarkly flag.

In Scope:
Replace the full-page Celebration screen with a non-blocking snack-bar component for all distinct scenarios listed in the Scope table. Confetti animation appears with the snack bar for positive celebratory scenarios and respects prefers-reduced-motion. Reward-type awareness: snack bar renders hearts, gems, or no reward icon depending on the trigger payload. Delayed-reward messaging for HC scenarios , communicating the 1-2 week or 5-6 week wait window. Mental-health branch: positive mood check -> content recommendation CTA in the snack bar; negative mood check -> emergency-resources CTA with no confetti and neutral styling. Drum-roll pre-reveal animation (scenario 15) plays inline before the snack bar appears, not as a full-page takeover. LaunchDarkly flag controls the entire refresh, allowing per-environment (QA / UAT / Production) and gradual rollout. Amplitude instrumentation for snack-bar impressions, CTA taps, auto-dismiss, and manual dismiss across all scenarios.

Accessibility:
ARIA live region announcement, keyboard dismissal, screen-reader parity (VoiceOver / TalkBack), WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, and minimum 44×44 touch targets. Suppression of legacy celebration modal, Badge/Tier full-page overlays previously tied to the old Celebration flow, and any duplicate confetti when the snack bar is active.

Out of Scope:
Redesign of the reward system itself (hearts, gems, tier logic, claim eligibility rules). Back-end changes to HC claims or document-upload reward calculation windows. New celebration triggers beyond the listed scenarios. Changes to the Badge / Tier earning logic - only the visual celebration treatment is suppressed. Email, push, or SMS celebration notifications. Localization of new copy beyond existing supported locales (English only at launch).

Use Cases:
A member completes a Pathway goal check-in and sees a snack bar confirming +hearts without leaving the Pathway screen . A member finishes a Pathway level or the full Pathway and receives unified snack-bar acknowledgment . A member completes an HC claims-based activity and is told via snack bar that their reward will arrive in 5-6 weeks. A member uploads an HC document and is told via snack bar that their reward will arrive in 1-2 weeks. A member rates an Explore item (Video / Audio / Article / Recipe / Wellness Webinar) and sees a snack bar confirming hearts or gems earned. A member hits a Challenge milestone and is celebrated inline without leaving the challenge view . A member submits a positive mood check-in and is offered relevant content recommendations in the snack bar. A member submits a negative mood check-in and is gently pointed to emergency resources in a non-celebratory snack bar. A member earning a reward sees a brief drum-roll animation before the snack bar reveals the outcome . A QA / product engineer toggles the LaunchDarkly flag in QA, UAT, or Production and verifies the new treatment without code redeploy. A screen-reader user hears the snack-bar content announced via an ARIA live region and can dismiss it via keyboard.

Assumptions:
The existing snack-bar component from F233336 (Explore Celebration Refresh) is reusable and will be extended, not rebuilt, for the remaining scenarios. A single LaunchDarkly flag will gate the refresh; scenario-level sub-flags are not required for launch but will be discussed with UX. The reward payload (type, amount, delayed-reward window) is provided by existing back-end services without API changes. Confetti assets and animation timings follow the reduced-motion guidelines established for F233336. Mental-health emergency-resource content is sourced from the existing resource catalog maintained by the Clinical team. Scenario 16 (Coaching) UX copy and reward mapping will be confirmed by the Coaching product stream before development completion. Amplitude event taxonomy will extend existing celebration events with a 'surface: snack_bar' property rather than introducing a new event family. acceptance aligns with WCAG 2.1 AA; VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android) are the reference screen readers. Summary: mDL Identity Verification
Description:

Problem Statement:
MAH currently relies on Mobile Network Operator (MNO)-based identity proofing and one-time passcode (OTP) challenges to perform step-up authentication for sensitive post-login actions. This approach is limited to members who have a phone number on file and does not provide a high-assurance identity verification signal. Additionally, OTP-based verification remains dependent on phone ownership and may be vulnerable to risks such as SIM-swap attacks or message interception.As a result, there is a coverage gap for members who cannot be verified through MNO-based methods or who require stronger identity assurance before performing sensitive actions. Currently, MAH does not provide a mechanism to verify identity using a government-issued credential.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If myActiveHealth introduces Mobile Driver's License (mDL) verification as an alternative step-up authentication method, then members can verify their identity using a higher-assurance government-issued credential stored in Apple Wallet or Google Wallet. This will expand verification coverage beyond phone-dependent methods, improve confidence in sensitive transactions, and allow the organization to evaluate member adoption and usability before considering broader deployment or future OTP replacement.

Summary: Enabler - Rewards Resolution Assistant
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Rewards-related inquiries represent the largest category of member support requests within MyActiveHealth. Recent incident ticket analysis shows that many rewards issues are not true system defects, but repeatable questions caused by limited visibility, unclear program rules, processing timelines, eligibility requirements, and redemption expectations.Members frequently contact support to understand why points are missing or delayed, whether an activity has been completed, what rewards they are eligible for, how to redeem rewards, or when they can expect to receive a payout. Because rewards programs can vary by client, program type, incentive model, activity rules, and payout method, members currently lack a centralized, self-service capability that can provide accurate answers based on their specific rewards configuration.As a result, routine and explainable questions often become support tickets, creating unnecessary operational overhead, increasing resolution time, and reducing member confidence in the rewards experience.MyActiveHealth needs a program-aware Rewards Resolution Assistant that can guide members through a predefined set of high-frequency rewards questions and provide the latest applicable answers based on their program type, reward status, and activity completion information.

Benefit Hypothesis:
If MyActiveHealth introduces a guided, program-aware Rewards Resolution Assistant that provides accurate answers to the most common rewards questions, then members will be able to self-serve routine rewards inquiries without contacting support.This will improve member transparency and trust in the rewards experience, reduce avoidable Rewards/Incentive support tickets, decrease operational overhead for support teams, and allow product and engineering teams to focus on true defects and higher-value enhancements.Success will be measured by:Reduction in Rewards/Incentive support ticket volumeIncrease in self-service completion rate for rewards inquiriesDecrease in repeat or duplicate rewards-related contactsImproved member satisfaction with rewards clarity and guidanceReduction in support escalations for routine program rule or status questions

Contacts/Dependencies:

In Scope:
Create a Phase 1 Rewards Resolution Assistant within MyActiveHealth focused on guided self-service support for rewards-related questions.Provide members with a predefined set of high-frequency rewards questions based on recent incident ticket patterns.Tailor answers based on the member's rewards program type and configuration.Support program-aware responses for key rewards variables, including:Dollar or Points or hearts-based programsGift card-based programsHRA/HSA payout programsPaycheck or employer-funded payout programsPrograms with no incentive configuredReporting ONLY INCV program.Provide guided answers for common rewards questions, including:Missing or delayed points/hearts/DollarPending activity creditCompleted vs. remaining reward activitiesReward eligibilityReward redemption processGift card or payout timingMaximum reward limitsProgram year and deadline guidanceDisplay member-specific reward information where available, including:Current reward balanceCompleted activitiesPending activitiesRemaining eligible activitiesReward type or payout methodProgram year informationUse controlled, predefined response templates to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance.Provide clear next steps when the assistant cannot resolve the inquiry through self-service.Escalate members to the appropriate support path when the question requires manual review or data correction.

Out of Scope:
Open-ended, free-form AI chatbot experience in Phase 1.AI-generated responses without predefined and approved templates.Automatic reward adjustments, manual overrides, or points corrections.Backend changes to reward calculation, reward eligibility, or payout processing logic.Replacing existing support teams or support workflows.Resolving complex edge cases that require manual investigation.Processing uploads or proof-of-completion documents in Phase 1.Real-time vendor issue remediation or vendor-side ticket creation.Proactive notifications or alerts for missing points, restored points, or pending activities.Full natural language intent detection across all possible rewards questions.Support for non-rewards-related MyActiveHealth issues, such as login, device sync, coaching, or general account support, unless directly tied to rewards guidance.

Summary: AHM BoB End-to-End testing - data sourced from Unified Onboarding Platform
Description:
Participants:
Prakash, Ravi, Ananda, Ray, John Israel, Adil, Junaid, Shenyan, Jordan, Andrew Z, Sai, Chintan, Jennifer, Priya, Jay, Rohith, Sridevi, Divyank, Veda & Jude, Ajith, Naziba, Sachin, Sundar, Anu, Arun, Rajesh, Mrudula, Maha, Alen, Eric, Mothi, Kishore, Arun, Mohd, Ganesh, Nithya, SendilRTE/PM: MeetaBusiness Lead: Jennifer Daniels, Lynette This feature tracks and enables participation of all ActiveHealth Management (AHM) products and their associated applications in Book of Business (BoB) end-to-end (E2E) testing, using data sourced from the Unified Onboarding Platform. The Unified Onboarding Platform serves as the single source of truth for onboarding data and configurations required to support client implementations across AHM product lines, including but not limited to AHM, TDC, and Weight Management. The specific scope of this feature is to ensure that AHM products are fully onboarded to Unified Onboarding Platform and can reliably consume onboarding data to support comprehensive E2E testing of Book of Business scenarios. This includes validating data readiness, integration points, and downstream application participation required for successful testing execution. E2E timeline: Entire month of August (8/3 to 8/31)

Benefit Hypothesis:
Improved Test Coverage & Participation VisibilityIf all AHM products and associated applications are onboarded through the Unified Onboarding Platform for Book of Business (BoB) E2E testing,then we will achieve complete visibility into participation status,resulting in improved test coverage and reduced risk of missed integrations. Early Detection of Integration GapsIf participation tracking is enforced before and during E2E testing,then missing integrations or incomplete onboarding will be identified early,resulting in fewer defects in downstream environments and production. Reduction in Data Inconsistencies Across SystemsIf BoB E2E testing data is sourced from a single unified onboarding platform,then inconsistencies caused by fragmented data sources will decrease,resulting in higher data accuracy across downstream applications (MAH, Care Engine, Epic, etc.). Faster Onboarding and Test Execution CyclesIf participation tracking is centralized and standardized,then product and application onboarding into BoB testing will be faster and more streamlined,resulting in reduced cycle time for end-to-end validation. Enhanced Accountability and TraceabilityIf participation status of each AHM product/application is explicitly tracked,then ownership gaps and unclear responsibilities will be minimized,resulting in improved accountability across Product, Engineering, and QA teams. Improved Reporting for Leadership & GovernanceIf participation metrics are captured centrally,then leadership will have real-time visibility into testing readiness and gaps,resulting in better decision-making and governance over BoB readiness. Summary: MMAH: Reprocessing the digital activities on member move within a same plan sponsor in an automated manner(the new supplier is part of a different incentive program)
Description:
Participants:
Mrudala , Arun , Eric , Mothi , Sudhakar , Sridevi , Mohd , Phalguni , Sheela , Parthibanand , Victoria , Jay , Subhro , Venkatkrishna Majjiga , Eswaran, Alen, Maha, ManavTech Lead: Eric LoB: All Variants Platform: <Web, iOS, Android>

Business Value:
Accurate Reward Allocation : Ensures members receive the correct reward amount based on program rules, dates, and configurations.Enhanced Member Experience: Members see consistent and fair reward outcomes, improving engagement and trust in wellness programs. Supports personalized incentives when program configurations change.Reporting Integrity : Accurate reporting to clientsImproves Operational Efficiency- Streamlines reward processing mechanism by Reprocessing the digital activities on member movement

Problem Statement:
When a member move across different suppliers, within the same plan sponsor (within same or different programs), member's completed activities, in progress activities and rewards/incentives are often not carried over. Given the members, are working with the same plan sponsor (employer), progress and completion should be retained as is and they should not see any change whatsoever in their account. Refer Defect: DE370397: Incentive Supplier Movement rollover is not working | Rally Scope: Reprocessing of digital activities shall be limited to the scenario when a member moves from one supplier to another within the same plan sponsor, either within the same INCV program or a different one.

Out of Scope:
Member move across different plan sponsor is out of scope as this is considered an employer change and member account will reset as per existing implementation.External activities and file based completions - These are already being processed for supplier change scenarios, under existing implementation and no change is being requested to this process.Scenarios and Requirements:When a member moves from one supplier to another, within the same plan sponsor and within the same incentive programAssumption - Given the incentive program remains the same, all the goals and activities available to a member, along with rewards setup, will remain the same across previous and new supplierThis is considered a move within the current employer and all member activities including (completed, in progress and not started) shall be carried over and be visible for the member under the new supplierSystem shall reprocess the activities such thatActivities 'completed' under supplier 1 are visible to the member under supplier 2 with original completion dates - no difference in member experienceActivities that were 'In-Progress' under supplier 1 are visible to the member under supplier 2 and the progress shall be saved and carried over - no difference in member experienceActivities that were 'Not started' under supplier 1 are visible to the member under supplier 2 and they shall continue to show in their original state under supplier 1 (not started) - no difference in member experienceAny rewards (irrespective of reward type and redemption type) earned by the member under supplier 1 (full or partial earning) shall be carried over to supplier 2 - no difference in member experienceVeda: Any movement to a ""Temp"" supplier (like ODS to GCP or similar reasons), the activities and rewards shall carry over as listed above.Product ""variant"" is expected to be common for all suppliers across a given program and hence no special considerations are defined with respect to variant, for this scenario. When a member moves from one supplier to another, within the same plan sponsor BUT, the new supplier is part of a different incentive programAssumption - Different incentive program may have a very different setup in terms of available activities, incentive eligible activities, the reward type and redemption types being offered etc.Assumption - Look back dates don't apply to digital activitiesAssumption - Completion date for activities will remain as is and incentive will only reprocess these activities as per rules defined below and not update the completion dates or status at allSuch an move is still considered a move within the current employer however, given the new program may have a completely different setup - a more nuanced approach is needed for handling different scenarios: System shall reprocess the activities such that: Activities that are common to both programsActivity Availability - If the activity is available as a valid activity under Program 1 + Supplier 1 AND the same activity is available under Program 2 + Supplier 2Such activities shall be available / visible to the member in their new program and supplier, with their current state (completed, in progress or not started)Shall carry over original completion dates for completed activitiesRewards - Member shall be rewarded for such common activities, even after the move, but subject to the rules of new programIf the activity completion date falls within the reward eligible window (i.e. it falls within the start and end dates for being eligible for a reward) under the new program AND member falls within the participant types to which the new program is offered, member shall be rewarded as per new program setup,This shall honor the configurations of new program including but not limited to participant types, goals, currency / reward type, redemption type etc.If the activity completion date falls outside the reward eligible window (i.e. it falls outside the start and end dates for being eligible for a reward) under the new program, member shall NOT be rewarded for such activities and any rewards earned under previous program will be forfeitedFamily Max should be carried forward under new supplier with different incentive program. Supplier 1 , program 1 -Family Max $100, Activities completed-$150 , New supplier 2 , program 2-Family Max-$300 , carry over will be $150 and reapply the Family Max limit as per new supplier configuration.Family Max should be carried forward under new supplier with different incentive program. Supplier 1 , program 1 -Family Max $300, Activities completed-$350 , New supplier 2 , program 2-Family Max-$100 , We cannot cap down the value , it should be $100. No negative balance should be reported.Runoff reports - Runoff from previous program will continue to show the earnings from previous program if such a runoff report was setup. These amount will not be reversed or dropped from the report. Activities that are available under previous program but NOT available under the new program (suppressed)Activity Availability - If the activity is available as a valid activity under Program 1 + Supplier 1 BUT the same activity is NOT available under Program 2 + Supplier 2Such activities shall NOT be available/visible to the member in their new program and supplier, as such activities are not supported by the new program.Rewards - Member shall be NOT be rewarded for such activities, as such activity are not at all applicable or available under the new programAny rewards earned under previous program will be forfeited and shall not be part of member's current balance any more.Runoff reports - Runoff from previous program will continue to show the earnings from previous program if such a runoff report was setup. These amount will not be reversed or dropped from the report. Activities that are NOT available under previous program but are available under the new programActivity Availability - Members shall be able to see all such activities that are offered by the new programs Rewards - Members shall be able to complete such activities and get rewarded as per the setup of this new program. Rollover ScenariosRollover is enabled in both programsIf Currency type, conversion ratio and Redemption type is sameCarry over the rollover amount and expiration period.If any of Currency type, conversion ratio or Redemption type is differentGiven the rollover amount is already converted and stored as $ value, we shall still be able to rollover the amount as is along with expiration period.Needs additional impact analysis by engineering , just to make sure this well covered.Rollover is enabled under current supplier and member has a balance but the new supplier doesn't have rollover enabledSystem will not support or carry over any rollover balanceMember would be expected to redeem these before moving over - Account management may have to handle this outside the system if neededRollover is NOT enabled under current supplier and member has a balance but the new supplier doesn't have rolloverNothing to carry overMothi - 2/25 - Rollover amount calculation under previous program may not automatically get calculated already, as a design, we may need to first calculate the rollover amount under previous supplier and then reprocess it under new supplier. Variant Considerations:Product variant is expected to be common across programs and suppliers under a plan sponsor - As variant is defined at a plan sponsor level.However, there are possible exceptions to this where mid year changes to variant occur though extremely rare. Confirmed with business (Lynette) that system doesn't need to support these in an automated fashion and handling of such scenarios will vary from case to case and account mgmt. + business will need to take care of them manually while making such changes (there are many other things to take care of when such exceptions are taken up and this is just one aspect) Reporting ScenariosCurrently, such member movements are already happening just that they are processed manually by S&O team and reporting is handling the movement (albeit there are some defects like DE375553). With this in mind, the change upstream to automate the manual process should not change anything at downstream. However, these are the expectations from business to ensure this is in place and tested.Runoff reports - Expected behavior against certain scenarios are noted aboveActivitiesAny completed under previous supplier will now show completed under the new supplier.The reports of previous supplier will not show these transactions anymorePayments/EarningsAll things equal, member shall not be have duplicate payments for completionsIf there is a difference in eligible earnings for already completed activities which results in a difference in earnings:Eligible earning for an activity is HIGHER under the new supplier (Supplier 2) than previous supplier (supplier 1) - Calculate the delta and pay the member for the difference under supplier 2.Eligible earning for an activity is LOWER under the new supplier (Supplier 2) than previous supplier (supplier 1) - Already paid amount will not be reverted back or adjusted. Already Redeemed rewards under previous programIf a member has already redeemed some rewards under previous program which would otherwise be forfeited upon move to new program (where the supplier move is across programs) - what should be expected behavior? Do we reduce the member balance in new program? What if it get's to a negative balance? Or do we ""exempt"" such redemption from forfeiting logic?Answer: We do not want to revert or reduce the balance by the amount but this can get complicated depending on the scenarios:The amount in new program can be same, higher or lower than previous program - consider all scenarios to define the expected behavior in case of redemption.If the newly calculated amount is higher than previous programEarned $50 in prv prgm - revaluated in new to $100 - if they already redeemed $25 - Their new balance should be (100 - 25 = $75)If the newly calculated amount is lower than previous programIf member earned $100 for 5 activities under Program 1 and redeemed $50. Now as per new program if we reprocess all 5 activities let's say the total $ amount would be $25 (because of a different conversion ratio). What should we do?We set this to $0 as new balance - no scenario shall lead to negative balance but we should not double pay the member as well (in this example they have already redeemed more than $25 and so no more payment)If the newly calculated amount is same as previous programIf member earned $100 for 5 activities under Program 1 and redeemed $50. Now as per new program if we reprocess all 5 activities let's say the total $ amount would be $100 (because of a different conversion ratio). What should we do?We subtract the redeemed amount show the rest as balance ($100 - 25) = 75For reporting scenarios, it will need to be considered with reporting team for different situations. Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Wellness Webinar Incentive Activity:Currently, members can complete unlimited recorded wellness webinars and earn rewards for each completion. Current behavior allows members to earn rewards for multiple webinar completions based on the configured occurrence count, but clients want the ability to restrict earnings frequency on a monthly basis.Tracker Incentive activity:Tracker incentives currently accumulate rewards daily throughout the program year. Current behavior allows members to continue earning rewards daily throughout the program year, which can exceed client budget expectations.

Benefit Hypothesis:
Improves configuration flexibility for Elite clients.Provides greater control over incentive budgets.Supports client-specific reward strategies.Responds to increasing client demand for configurable earning restrictions.Improved member transparency regarding earning opportunities.Simplified incentive configuration.Reduced need for complex reward calculations.Improved member engagement and understanding.

Summary: Termed Supplier and Member Handling with Tracker Sync Prevention
Description:
Problem Statement (Who, What, Where, When, Why):
Two issues with termed supplier/member re: tracker sync prevention (impact: may cause delay/slowness) Issue 1: Termination status for suppliers and members is not consistently received, which prevents us from reliably stopping tracker data synchronization. Next steps for Issue 1:Need to identify current process for termination and when/where gap occurs Issue 2: Even when termination status is received, tracker data continues to sync in certain scenarios (e.g., DE373293: tracker data continues to sync despite the member being termed). Impact: These gaps create a legal and compliance risk, as data may continue to sync for suppliers or members who should no longer be processed. Short term fix for issue 2:S&O: Pick the termed members and disconnect their tracker device from backendBy 2/20, this will be completedLong term fix for issue 2:Analysis requested by business to understand impact Prevent any Tracker data from syncing to MAH for termed members/supplier while preserving auditability and minimizing operational overhead. Option 1 - CDPApproach: Use CDP (which already processes Validic data) to filter out events for termed members/suppliers and prevent forwarding data to MAHPros:Leverages existing CDP pipelines and member-status enrichmentNo application or backend changes requiredNear real-time behavior once member status is updated in CDPCons:Data from tracker devices is still sent from ValidicAlthough data is not visible in the MAH app for termed members, ingestion continues at the source level. Estimate - 30 pointsOption 2 - Digital batch disconnect (Digital and CDP)Approach: Implement a daily batch job to identify connected, termed members/suppliers and trigger a backend disconnect to stop future data ingestion from ValidicProsFully stops future data ingestion at the sourceCleaner long-term solution for data governanceCon:Additional complexity: new pub/sub implementation, backend logic, and monitoring required.EstimateCDP - 40 pointsDigital - 30 points Termed Historical DataThe S&O team will need to execute a one-time cleanup job
